method: Same-agent bilingual close reading and reverse paraphrase of each theorem, reduction, complement construction and proof-enumeration argument; exact formula, macro, glossary-token and reference checks after one bounded source-correction projection. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Unsolvability of first-order validity, undecidability of satisfiability and one-sided semidecidability of validity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A hypothetical always-halting validity decider D would receive the effective encoding of a machine M_e and word w as the sentence !T(M_e,w) implies !E(M_e,w). Composing the encoder E with D would decide whether M_e halts on w, contradicting the earlier halting theorem.
samples.checks: Both 1 and 0 output branches, the always-halting requirement, the composition order E then D and both verification-lemma references are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A satisfiability decider S would decide validity by prefixing negation to the input sentence, running S, and reversing its one-stroke yes/no result. A sentence is valid exactly when its negation is unsatisfiable.
samples.checks: The right-shift and square-one negation operation, the two satisfiability outputs, the stroke erasure/writing cases and the final complement relation remain exact. OLTUR-016 consistently names the input !B.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Validity has no always-halting yes/no decider, but it has a one-sided recognizer. Effective enumeration of all derivations finds a proof of B exactly when B is valid: soundness prevents a false positive and completeness ensures eventual discovery of a proof when B is valid.
samples.checks: The no-instance diverges, the yes-instance halts with 1, and soundness/completeness are used in the correct directions. The distinct semantic entailment and syntactic provability formulas are preserved.

source_observations: OLTUR-016: the frozen satisfiability proof first calls the input B but immediately shifts !B and consistently reasons about !B; the Marathi uses !B at the first mention.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
